```python
    :param value:
    :type value: timedelta
    :return:
    """

    days = value.days

    minutes = (value.seconds // 60) % 60
```

```python
def protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
    """ Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
    keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
    provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
    depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
    version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

    :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
            version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
    :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
            relevant and supported protocol versions
    :raise TypeError: if protocol version is not passed in a tuple
    """
    if protocol_version is not None:
        if not isinstance(protocol_version, tuple):
            raise TypeError("protocol_version must be a tuple")
        # Use this dictionary to map versions to their respective handler classes
        known_handlers = {
            (3, 5): BoltProtocolHandler35,
            (3, 4): BoltProtocolHandler34
        }
        handler_class = known_handlers.get(protocol_version, None)
        if handler_class is None:
            raise NotImplementedError("Unsupported protocol version " + str(protocol_version))
    else:
        # This list should contain all the supported protocol handlers
        handler_classes = [BoltProtocolHandler35, BoltProtocolHandler34, BoltProtocolHandler21]
        handler_dict = {cls, None}
        for handler in handler_classes:
            handler_dict[handler] = handler
    return handler_dict
```

```python
    @classmethod
    def protocol_handlers(cls, protocol_version=None):
        """ Return a dictionary of available Bolt protocol handlers,
        keyed by version tuple. If an explicit protocol version is
        provided, the dictionary will contain either zero or one items,
        depending on whether that version is supported. If no protocol
        version is provided, all available versions will be returned.

        :param protocol_version: tuple identifying a specific protocol
            version (e.g. (3, 5)) or None
        :return: dictionary of version tuple to handler class for all
            relevant and supported protocol versions
        :raise TypeError: if protocol_version is not passed in a tuple
        """
        supported_versions = getattr(cls, 'NATIVE_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS', [])
        if protocol_version is None:
            return {version: handler for version, handler in supported_versions.items()}

        version, desired_major, desired_minor = protocol_version
        if version not in supported_versions:
            raise ValueError(f" unrecognized protocol version {protocol_version}, valid versions are {supported_versions}")

        handler = supported_versions[version]
        if (desired_major, desired_minor) != handler.version:
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported protocol version {protocol_version}, required {handler.version} but recommended is {desired_major}.{desired_minor}")

        return {protocol_version: handler}
```

```python
def unit_of_work(metadata=None, timeout=None):
    """This function is a decorator for transaction functions that allows extra control over how the transaction is carried out.

    For example, a timeout may be applied::

        from neo4j import unit_of_work

        @unit_of_work(timeout=100)
        def count_people_tx(tx):
            result = tx.run("MATCH (a:Person) RETURN count(a) AS persons")
            record = result.single()
            return record["persons"]

    :param metadata:
        a dictionary with metadata.
        Specified metadata will be attached to the executing transaction and visible in the output of ``dbms.listQueries`` and ``dbms.listTransactions`` procedures.
        It will also get logged to the ``query.log``.
        This functionality makes it easier to tag transactions and is equivalent to ``dbms.setTXMetaData`` procedure, see https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/reference/procedures/ for procedure reference.
    :type metadata: dict

    :param timeout:
        the transaction timeout in seconds.
        Transactions that execute longer than the configured timeout will be terminated by the database.
        This functionality allows to limit query/transaction execution time.
        Specified timeout overrides the default timeout configured in the database using ``dbms.transaction.timeout`` setting.
        Value should not represent a negative duration.
        A zero duration will make the transaction execute indefinitely.
        None will use the default timeout configured in the database.
    :type timeout: float or :const:`None`
    """
    def decorator(func):
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            if metadata is not None:
                tx = args[0].session.transaction_meta(metadata)
            elif timeout is not None:
                tx = args[0].session.transaction(timeout=timeout)
            else:
                tx = args[0].session.transaction()

            try:
                return func(tx, *args, **kwargs)
            finally:
                txCommit(tx)
        return wrapper
    return decorator
```

```python
def data(self, *keys):
    """ Return the keys and values of this record as a dictionary,
        optionally including only certain values by index or key. Keys
        provided in the items that are not in the record will be
        inserted with a value of :const:`None`; indexes provided
        that are out of bounds will trigger an :exc:`IndexError`.

        :param keys: indexes or keys of the items to include; if none
                      are provided, all values will be included
        :return: dictionary of values, keyed by field name
        :raises: :exc:`IndexError` if an out-of-bounds index is specified
        """
    values = {}
    for key in keys:
        if key in self:
            values[key] = self[key]
        elif key is None:
            values[key] = None
        else:
            raise KeyError("Invalid key provided to data: " + str(key))
```

```python
def pop_u16(self):
    """ Remove the last two bytes of data, returning them as a big-endian
    16-bit unsigned integer.
    """
    # Check if there are enough bytes to pop 16 bits
    if len(self) < 2:
        raise ValueError("Not enough bytes to pop 16 bits")

    # Pop the last two bytes
    bytes = self[-2:]
    data = bytes[1] << 8 | bytes[0]
    self.pop()

    return data
```

```python
def round_half_to_even(n):
    """Round a number to the nearest integer, rounding half to even.

        For example:
        >>> round_half_to_even(3)
        3
        >>> round_half_to_even(3.2)
        3
        >>> round_half_to_even(3.5)
        4
        >>> round_half_to_even(3.7)
        4
        >>> round_half_to_even(4)
        4
        >>> round_half_to_even(4.2)
        4
        >>> round_half_to_even(4.5)
        4
        >>> round_half_to_even(4.7)
        5
    """

    # Handle cases where the fractional part is exactly 0.5
    if n * 2 % 1 == 0.5:
        return int(round(n))
    # Handle the rest of the cases
    else:
        return int(round(n)) + (-1 if n < 0 else 1)
```

```python
import os

def xargs(
        cmd: tuple[str, ...],
        varargs: Sequence[str],
        *,
        color: bool = False,
        target_concurrency: int = 1,
        _max_length: int = _get_platform_max_length(),
        **kwargs: Any,
) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    """A simplified implementation of xargs.

    color: Make a pty if on a platform that supports it
    target_concurrency: Target number of partitions to run concurrently
    """

    # Check if the system supports colorization with pty
    if color and os.name == 'posix':
        import pty
        master, slave = pty.fork()

        def read_stdin():
            return os.read(master, _max_length)

        def write_stdout(data):
            os.write(slave, data)

        def write_stderr(data):
            os.write(master, data)

        os.setraw(slave, os.FIONJECT)
        os.close(master)

        promises = []
        for i in range(target_concurrency):
            _, stdin, stdout, stderr = os.popen4([str(x) for x in cmd] + ["|", str(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "xargs_read")) + "> stdout | " + str(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "xargs_write")) + " 2>&1"])
            promise = {
                'stdin': stdin,
                'stdout': stdout,
                'stderr': stderr,
                'read_stdin': read_stdin,
                'write_stdout': write_stdout,
                'write_stderr': write_stderr,
                'pid': os.getpid(),
            }
            promises.append(promise)

        results = []
        for i, promise in enumerate(promises):
            stdout = b''
            stderr = b''
            for line in iter(promise['read_stdin'], b''):
                if os.read(promise['stdin'], 1) == b'\x1b':
                    continue
                stdout += line
            for line in iter(promise['read_stderr'], b''):
                if os.read(promise['stdin'], 1) == b'\x1b':
                    continue
                stderr += line
            results.append((promise['pid'], stdout, stderr, i))

        os.close(slave)

        status = 0
        for pid, stdout, stderr, index in results:
            result_status, output = os.popen4([str(x) for x in cmd] + ["|", str(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "xargs_pid")) + "> stdout | " + str(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "xargs_pid")) + " 2>&1"], stdin=os.open(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "xargs_" + str(pid) + "_" + str(index) + ".stdout"), 'rb'))
            result_status.close()
            stdout.close()
            if result_status.returncode != 0:
                status = -1

        return (status, stdout)
```

```python
import os

import sys
from typing import Sequence, Any
from .utils import _get_platform_max_length

def xargs(
        cmd: tuple[str, ...],
        varargs: Sequence[str],
        *,
        color: bool = False,
        target_concurrency: int = 1,
        _max_length: int = _get_platform_max_length(),
        **kwargs: Any,
) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    """A simplified implementation of xargs.

    color: Make a pty if on a platform that supports it
    target_concurrency: Target number of partitions to run concurrently
    """
    buffer = bytearray()
    pipe = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, shell=True)
    os.dup2(pipe.stdout.fileno(), sys.stdout.fileno())
    os.dup2(pipe.stderr.fileno(), sys.stderr.fileno())
    _max_length = max(_max_length, pipe.stddout.fileno())

    for var in varargs:
        if color:
            command = f"{cmd[0]} 2>&1 | colorize {cmd[0]} {var}"
        else:
            command = f"{cmd[0]} {var}"

        try:
            output, _ = pipe.communicate(command.encode(), max_length=_max_length)
            if output:
                buffer.extend(output)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            pipe.kill()
            output, _ = pipe.communicate(max_length=_max_length)
            if output:
                buffer.extend(output)

    return len(buffer), buffer
```

```python
def xargs(cmd: tuple[str, ...], varargs: Sequence[str], *, color: bool = False, target_concurrency: int = 1, _max_length: int = _get_platform_max_length(), **kwargs: Any) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    """A simplified implementation of xargs.

    color: Make a pty if on a platform that supports it
    target_concurrency: Target number of partitions to run concurrently
    """
    import subprocess
    import os
    
    # Escape special characters in the command
    escaped_cmd = ' '.join(subprocess.escape(part) for part in cmd)
    
    # Create a list of command parts to be executed in parallel
    parts = escaped_cmd.split()
    cmds = []
    current_part = []
    for part in parts:
        # If the current part is empty or ends with a space, split it
        if not current_part or part.endswith(' '):
            if current_part:
                cmds.append(' '.join(current_part))
                current_part = [part]
            else:
                current_part = [part]
        else:
            current_part.append(part)
    if current_part:
        cmds.append(' '.join(current_part))
    
    # Iterate over each command part in parallel
    all_processes = []
    for cmd in cmds:
        # If color is enabled and supported, open a PTY for the subprocess
        if color and os.name == 'posix':
            process = subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, preexec_fn=subprocess.start_new_session)
        else:
            process = subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True)
        all_processes.append(process)
    
    # Wait for all processes to complete
    exit_codes = []
    output_bytes = b''
    for process in all_processes:
        exit_code = process.wait()
        output_bytes += process.stdout.read()
        exit_codes.append(exit_code)
    
    return exit_codes, output_bytes
```

```python
    - windows does not parse shebangs
```

```python
def cached(cache, key=hashkey, lock=None):
    """Decorator to wrap a function with a memoizing callable that saves
    results in a cache.

    """

    def decorator(func):
        cache_value = cache.get(key)
        if cache_value is not None:
            return cache_value

        @wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            result = func(*args, **kwargs)
            cache.set(key, result)
```

```python
def cached(cache_function, key=lambda x: hash(x), lock=noop):
    result = {}
    lock = lock or threading.Lock()

    @functools.wraps(cache_function)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        # Retrieve the concatenated key for the memoization cache
        key = (key(*args), tuple(sorted(kwargs.items())))

        try:
            lock.acquire()
            # Return cached result if available
            return result[key]
        finally:
            lock.release()

        # Calculate the actual result
        result[key] = cache_function(*args, **kwargs)
        # Store updated cache
        return result[key]

    return wrapper
```

```python
from collections import OrderedDict

def lfu_cache(maxsize=128, typed=False):
    """Decorator to wrap a function with a memoizing callable that saves
    up to `maxsize` results based on a Least Frequently Used (LFU)
    algorithm.
    """
    cache = OrderedDict(maxsize=maxsize)

    def wrapper(*args):
        if args in cache:
            result = cache[args]
            cache.move_to_end(args)
            return result
        result = func(*args)
        cache[args] = result
        return result

    return wrapper
```

```python
                else:
```

```python
                    path_levels[i] = path_levels[i-1]

            for line in lines:
                try:
                    line_level = path_levels[path_levels.index(level)]
                    level = line_level + 1
                except ValueError:
                    level = breaks

                if level > max_level:

                parts = line.rsplit(maxsplit=max_path_level)
                if len(parts) > 1:
                    exception_str += ' - ' + ' '.join(parts[1:])
                    exception_value = parts[0]
```

```python
def _legacy_mergeOrderings(orderings):
    """Merge multiple orderings so that within-ordering order is preserved

    Orderings are constrained in such a way that if an object appears
    in two or more orderings, then the suffix that begins with the
    object must be in both orderings.

    For example:

    >>> _mergeOrderings([
    ... ['x', 'y', 'z'],
    ... ['q', 'z'],
    ... [1, 3, 5],
    ... ['z']
    ... ])
    ['x', 'y', 'q', 1, 3, 5, 'z']
    """
    merged = {}
    for ordering in orderings:
        for item in ordering:
            if item not in merged:
                merged[item] = []
            merged[item].extend(ordering)
    
    ordered = []
    for item, order in merged.items():
        ordered.extend(order)
    
    return ordered
```

```python
def _legacy_mergeOrderings(orderings):
    """Merge multiple orderings so that within-ordering order is preserved

    Orderings are constrained in such a way that if an object appears
    in two or more orderings, then the suffix that begins with the
    object must be in both orderings.

    For example:

    >>> _legacy_mergeOrderings([
    ... ['x', 'y', 'z'],
    ... ['q', 'z'],
    ... [1, 3, 5],
    ... ['z']
    ... ])
    ['x', 'y', 'q', 1, 3, 5, 'z']

    """
    orderings = [set(o) for o in orderings]

    to_merge = []
    for i, o in enumerate(orderings):
        for j, oj in enumerate(orderings):
            if i == j:
                continue
            if o.isdisjoint(oj):
                to_merge.append((i, j))

    for idx1, idx2 in to_merge:
        del orderings[idx1]
        orderings[idx2].update(orderings[idx1])  # merge orderings

    return [sorted(os) for os in orderings]
```

```python
    # Iterate through each class in the input list
```

```python
def minimalBases(classes):
    """Reduce a list of base classes to its ordered minimum equivalent"""
    from collections import defaultdict

    # Create a graph of knows relationships between classes
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    for c1, c2 in zip(classes, classes[1:]):
        graph[c1].append(c2)

    # Initialize a set to keep track of visited classes
    visited = set()

    # Perform a depth-first search to find the smallest set of classes that includes all of the original classes
    stack = [classes[0]]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        if node in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(node)
        stack.extend(graph[node])

    # Return the smallest set of classes
    return list(visited)
```

```python
def _update_context(self, context):
    """Update *context* with the properties of this graph.

    *context.error* is appended with indices of errors.
    Example subcontext for a graph with fields "E,t,error_E_low":
    {"error": {"x_low": {"index": 2}}}.
    Note that error names are called "x", "y" and "z"
    (this corresponds to first three coordinates,
    if they are present), which allows to simplify plotting.
    Existing values are not removed
    from *context.value* and its subcontexts.

    Called on "destruction" of the graph (for example,
    in :class:`.ToCSV`). By destruction we mean conversion
    to another structure (like text) in the flow.
    The graph object is not really destroyed in this process.
    """
    result = context.copy()  # shallow copy to avoid modifying original context
    result['error'] = result.get('error', {})
    
    # process 'E' and 't' fields
    if 'E' in self.__dict__:
        result['error']['E'] = {'index': self.fields['E'].index_it}
    if 't' in self.__dict__:
        result['error']['t'] = {'index': self.fields['t'].index_it}
    
    # handle error indices
    for key, value in result['error'].items():
        for k, v in value.items():
            if k != 'index':
                result['error'][key][k] = v
    
    return result
```

```python
    """Compute integral (scale for a histogram).

    *bins* contain values, and *edges* form the mesh
    for the integration.
    Their format is defined in :class:`.histogram` description.
    """
    if len(bins) != len(edges) + 1:
        raise ValueError("bins and edges must have the same length except for the zeroth element")
    integral = 0
    for i in range(len(bins) - 1):
        integral += bins[i+1] - bins[i]
    return integral
```

```python
def difference(d1, d2, level=-1):
    """Return a dictionary with items from *d1* not contained in *d2*.

    *level* sets the maximum depth of recursion. For infinite recursion,
    set that to -1. For level 1,
    if a key is present both in *d1* and *d2* but has different values,
    it is included into the difference.
    See :func:`intersection` for more details.

    *d1* and *d2* remain unchanged. However, *d1* or some of its
    subdictionaries may be returned directly.
    Make a deep copy of the result when appropriate.

    .. versionadded:: 0.5
       add keyword argument *level*.
    """
    if not level:  # base case: if level is 0 or below, return the full dictionary
        return copy.deepcopy(d1)
    
    diff = {key: value for key, value in d1.items() if key not in d2}
    
    for key, value in d1.items():
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            nested_diff = difference(value, d2, level-1)
            if nested_diff:
                diff[key] = nested_diff
    
    return diff
```

```python
def generate_default_observer_schema_dict(manifest_dict, first_level=False):
    """Together with :func:``generate_default_observer_schema_list``, this function is
    called recursively to generate part of a default ``observer_schema`` from part of a
    Kubernetes resource, defined respectively by ``manifest_dict`` or ``manifest_list``.

    Args:
        manifest_dict (dict): Partial Kubernetes resources
        first_level (bool, optional): If True, indicates that the dictionary represents
            the whole observer schema of a Kubernetes resource

    Returns:
        dict: Generated partial observer_schema

    This function creates a new dictionary from ``manifest_dict`` and replaces all
    non-list and non-dict values by ``None``.

    In case of ``first_level`` dictionary (i.e. complete ``observer_schema`` for a
    resource), the values of the identifying fields are copied from the manifest file.
    """
    observer_schema = {}
    for key, value in manifest_dict.items():
        if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
            observer_schema[key] = generate_default_observer_schema_dict(value, first_level)
        else:
            observer_schema[key] = None

    # Copy identifying fields
    if first_level:
```

```python
    Returns a :class:`tuple` containing:

    -	The formatted SQL query (:class:`str` or :class:`bytes`).
```

```python
    -	A :class:`list` containing each set of converted out-style
            parameters (:class:`dict` or :class:`list`).
```

```python
    formattedsql = self.sql[:]
    for (setnum,many_params_set) in enumerate(many_params):
        params = many_params_set
        result = []
        if self.SQLParams.in_style ==airesql.SQLParams.NAMED:
            for k,v in params.items():

            for v in params:

                result.append(v)
                i += 1
        many_params_set = result
        many_params_list.append(many_params_set)
    return formattedsql, many_params_list
```

```python
def formatmany(self, sql: AnyStr, many_params: Union[Iterable[Dict[str, Any]], Iterable[Sequence[Any]]]) -> Tuple[AnyStr, Union[List[Dict[str, Any]], List[Sequence[Any]]]]:
    converted_sql = sql
    converted_params = [p.copy() for p in many_params]
    for idx, params in enumerate(converted_params):
        for key, value in params.items():
            if self.SQLParams.in_style == 'named':  # Handle named parameter style
                converted_sql = converted_sql.replace('%(' + key + ')s', "' + value + '" if isinstance(value, str) else str(value))
            elif self.SQLParams.in_style == 'ordinal':  # Handle ordinal parameter style
                converted_params[idx][key] = f"'{value}'" if isinstance(value, str) else str(value)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported in-style: {self.SQLParams.in_style}")
    return converted_sql, converted_params
```

```python
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

def _eval_file(prefix, file_path):
    """
    Identifica o tipo de arquivo do pacote: `asset` ou `rendition`.

    Identifica o tipo de arquivo do pacote e atualiza `packages` com o tipo e
    o endereço do arquivo em análise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    prefix : str
        nome do arquivo XML sem extensão
    filename : str
        filename
    file_folder : str
        file folder

    Returns
    -------
    dict
    """
    file_path = os.path.join(file_folder, filename)
    tree = ET.parse(file_path)
    root = tree.getroot()

    for element in root.iter():
        package_type = element.find('package_type')
        if package_type is not None:
            package_type = package_type.text
            break

    packages[package_type] = {
        'filename': filename,
        'file_path': file_path
    }

    return packages
```

```python
    if basename in self.assets:

    try:

    self.assets[basename] = test_doc
```

```python
from xml.etree.ElementTree import Element, SubElement

def absorb(self, args: Sequence[Any]) -> Sequence[Any]:
    """
    Given an `args` sequence of expressions, return a new list of expression
    applying absorption and negative absorption.

    See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absorption_law

    Absorption::

        A & (A | B) = A, A | (A & B) = A

    Negative absorption::

        A & (~A | B) = A & B, A | (~A & B) = A | B
    """
    result = []
    for exp in args:
        new_exp = exp
        if exp in self.expressions:
            new_exp = exp | self.expressions[exp]
            self.expressions.pop(exp)
        result.append(new_exp)
        if not self.expressions:
            break
    return result
```

```python
def _fromutc(self, dt):
    """
    Given a timezone-aware datetime in a given timezone, calculates a
    timezone-aware datetime in a new timezone.

    Since this is the one time that we *know* we have an unambiguous
    datetime object, we take this opportunity to determine whether the
    datetime is ambiguous and in a "fold" state (e.g. if it's the first
    occurrence, chronologically, of the ambiguous datetime).
    
    :param dt:
        A timezone-aware :class:`datetime.datetime` object.
    """
    from datetime import timedelta
    
    # Determine the local datetime of the given datetime object
    local_datetime = dt.astimezone(self.config.timezone)
    
    # Determine the timezone offset of the new timezone
    new_timezone_offset = (self.config.timezone - self.timezone).total_seconds()
    
    # Calculate the new UTC datetime
    new_utc_datetime = local_datetime.astimezone(self.config.timezone).replace(tzinfo=None) + timedelta(seconds=new_timezone_offset)
    
    # Check for ambiguity and fold state
    is_fold = local_datetime.utcoffset() == new_utc_datetime.utcoffset()
    
    return dt.astimezone(self.config.timezone), new_utc_datetime.astimezone(self.config.timezone), is_fold
```

```python
import datetime

def _fromutc(self, dt):
    """
    Given a timezone-aware datetime in a given timezone, calculates a
    timezone-aware datetime in a new timezone.

    Since this is the one time that we *know* we have an unambiguous
    datetime object, we take this opportunity to determine whether the
    datetime is ambiguous and in a "fold" state (e.g. if it's the first
    occurrence, chronologically, of the ambiguous datetime).

    :param dt:
        A timezone-aware :class:`datetime.datetime` object.
    """
    selftz = dt.tzinfo
    to_tz = self.tzinfo

    if selftz == to_tz:
        # zero timedelta when already in target timezone, no change necessary
        return dt

    if selftz.utcoffset(dt.bytes) == to_tz.utcoffset(dt.bytes):
        # the same timezone as target, no change necessary
        return dt

    # dt is not in target timezone, calculate new timezone
    delta = selftz.utcoffset(dt.bytes) - to_tz.utcoffset(dt.bytes)

    # handle ambiguities and folds
    if delta > datetime.timedelta(seconds=-1) and delta < datetime.timedelta(seconds=1):
        # the Python datetime library doesn't handle this correctly
        # we manually handle this case
        if selftz._isutcoffsetnegative() != to_tz._isutcoffsetnegative():
            # the offset was negative or positive, which means we need to handle it
            # differently
            dt = dt + delta
            if dt.isocalendar()[2] == 1:
                dt -= datetime.timedelta(days=1)
            elif dt.isocalendar()[2] == 4:
                dt += datetime.timedelta(days=1)
            return dt
        else:
            # the offset was equal, but the tz is changing, so we need to move the datetime
            dt += delta
            return dt
    else:
        # the offset is different, so we need to move the datetime
        dt = dt + delta
        return dt
```

**Explanation**:
The `_fromutc` method calculates a timezone-aware datetime in a new timezone based on a given timezone-aware datetime in a target timezone. It handles ambiguities and folds as specified.

```python
def tzname_in_python2(namefunc):
    """Change unicode output into bytestrings in Python 2

    tzname() API changed in Python 3. It used to return bytes, but was changed
    to unicode strings
    """
    if not hasattr(io, 'TextIOWrapper'):
        return namefunc
    def wrapper(*args, **kw):
        with io.TextIOWrapper(*args, **kw, errors='surrogateescape') as file:
```

```python
def next_version(version):
    """Next version identifier following existing pattern.

    Must deal with both zero-prefixed and non-zero prefixed versions.
    """
    # Strips any leading zeros from the version number
    version = version.lstrip('0')
    
    # Checks if the version is zero
    if len(version) == 0:
        return "1"
    
    # Increments the version number by 1
    new_version = str(int(version) + 1).zfill(len(version))
    
    return new_version
```

```python
def parse_subparser_arguments(unparsed_arguments, subparsers):
    """
    Given a sequence of arguments and a dict from subparser name to argparse.ArgumentParser
    instance, give each requested action's subparser a shot at parsing all arguments. This allows
    common arguments like "--repository" to be shared across multiple subparsers.

    Return the result as a tuple of (a dict mapping from subparser name to a parsed namespace of
    arguments, a list of remaining arguments not claimed by any subparser).
    """
    arg_groups = {}
    remaining_arguments = []

    for name, parser in subparsers.items():
        args = parser.parse_known_args(unparsed_arguments)
        arg_groups[name] = args
        remaining_arguments.extend(args.args)

    return arg_groups, remaining_arguments
```

```python
def parse_subparser_arguments(unparsed_arguments, subparsers):
    # If no arguments are provided, return two empty dictionaries
    if len(unparsed_arguments) == 0:
        return {}, []

    # Create a dictionary to hold the parsed arguments for each subparser
    parsed_arguments = {}
    # Create a list to hold any remaining arguments
    remaining_arguments = []

    # Iterate over the unmatched arguments and matches them to subparsers
    for arg in unparsed_arguments:
        for subparser_name, parser in subparsers.items():
            if parser.prog in arg:
                # Parse the arguments for the current subparser
                parsed_args = parser.parse_known_args(arg[parser.prog:])
                # Add the parsed arguments to the dictionary
                parsed_arguments[subparser_name] = parsed_args[0]
                # Remove the arguments from the list of unmatched arguments
                remaining_arguments.extend(parsed_args[1:])
                # Break out of the loop once a subparser is matched
                break

    return parsed_arguments, remaining_arguments
```

```python
def deep_merge_nodes(nodes):
    """
    Given a nested borgmatic configuration data structure as a list of tuples in the form of:

        (
            ruamel.yaml.nodes.ScalarNode as a key,
            ruamel.yaml.nodes.MappingNode or other Node as a value,
        ),

    ... deep merge any node values corresponding to duplicate keys and return the result. If
    there are colliding keys with non-MappingNode values (e.g., integers or strings), the last
    of the values wins.

    For instance, given node values of:

        [
            (
                ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
                MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                    (
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                    ),
                    (
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='7')
                    ),
                ]),
            ),
            (
                ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
                MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                    (
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                    ),
                ]),
            ),
        ]

    ... the returned result would be:

        [
            (
                ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='retention'),
                MappingNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:map', value=[
                    (
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_hourly'),
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='24')
                    ),
                    (
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:str', value='keep_daily'),
                        ScalarNode(tag='tag:yaml.org,2002:int', value='5')
                    ),
                ]),
            ),
        ]

    The purpose of deep merging like this is to support, for instance, merging one borgmatic
    configuration file into another for reuse, such that a configuration section ("retention",
    etc.) does not completely replace the corresponding section in a merged file.
    """
    merged_entries = defaultdict(dict)
    
    for key, value in nodes:
        merged_entries[key].update(value)
    
    merged_nodes = [(key, value) for key, value in merged_entries.items()]
    return merged_nodes
```

```python
from ruamel.yaml import MappingNode, ScalarNode, Node
from romanesco import AbstractElement, Document, AttributeError, DuplicateAnnotationError, DuplicateIDError

def deep_merge_nodes(nodes: List[Tuple[Node, MappingNode]]) -> List[Tuple[Node, MappingNode]]:
    merged_nodes = {}
    for value_node, map_node in nodes:
        key_values = merged_nodes.get(value_node, [])
        key_values.append((map_node, None))
        merged_nodes[value_node] = key_values

    result = []
    for value_node, key_values in merged_nodes.items():
        value_node_new = value_node.copy()
        for map_node, collocation in key_values:
            if isinstance(map_node, MappingNode):
                if map_node.tag.startswith('tag:yaml.org,2002:docinfo:'):
                    self.error('Cannot deep merge docinfo node', value_node_new)
                    continue
                collocation_value = collocation.copy()
                collocation_value.new_child(key_node)
            else:
                self.warning('Cannot deep merge non_mapping node', value_node_new)
                continue
            value_node_new.new_child(collocation_value)
        result.append((value_node_new, None))
    return result
```

```python
def parser_flags(parser):
    """
    Given an argparse.ArgumentParser instance, return its argument flags in a space-separated
    string.

    Args:
        parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): An instance of argparse.ArgumentParser

    Returns:
        str: A space-separated string of the argument flags
    """

    # Initialize an empty list to store the argument flags
    flags = []

    # Get all the arguments in the parser
    args = vars(parser.parse_args())

    # Iterate over the arguments
    for arg, value in args.items():
        # Append the argument flag to the list
        flags.append(arg)

    # Join the list of flags into a space-separated string and return it
    return ' '.join(flags)
```

```python
# borgmatic completion script

_borgmatic_completion() {{
    local c
    local subcommands=("location show lock create unlock load resurrect close merge split prune send sync serve mount unmount list status changelog search zip diff createlocation bulkcreate")
    local commands=("${subcommands[@]}")
    local args=({result_str:=${result_str:+ " "$result_str"))

        _init_completion -n 'COMP_WORDS' -n 'COMP_CWORD' -f commands$argspipes
    elif [[ $cur == * ]]; then

            local subcommands=("${!arg_values[@]}")
            _init_completion -n 'COMP_WORDS' -n 'COMP_CWORD' -f subcommands$argspipes
        else
            COMPREPLY=(${(f)"$command_values[@]"})
        fi
    fi
}}

complete -F _borgmatic_completion borgmatic'
```

```python
def parse_subparser_arguments(unparsed_arguments, subparsers):
"""Given a sequence of arguments and a dict from subparser name to argparse.ArgumentParser
 instance, give each requested action's subparser a shot at parsing all arguments. This allows
 common arguments like "--repository" to be shared across multiple subparsers.

Return the result as a tuple of (a dict mapping from subparser name to a parsed namespace of
 arguments, a list of remaining arguments not claimed by any subparser).

Arguments:
    unparsed_arguments (list): A list of command line arguments to parse.
    subparsers (dict): A dictionary mapping from subparser name to an argparse.ArgumentParser
                        instance.

Returns:
    tuple: A tuple containing two elements:
        1. A dictionary mapping from subparser name to an argparse.Namespace object containing the parsed arguments.
        2. A list of remaining command line arguments.
    """
    parsed_arguments = {}
    remaining_arguments = []

    for subparser in subparsers.values():
        try:
            namespace = subparser.parse_args(unparsed_arguments)
            parsed_arguments[subparser.name] = namespace
        except Exception as e:
            remaining_arguments.extend(unparsed_arguments)

    return parsed_arguments, remaining_arguments
```

```python
def size_to_bytes(size: str) -> int:
    """Convert human readable file size to bytes.

    Resulting value is an approximation as input value is in most case rounded.

    Args:
        size: A string representing a human readable file size (eg: '500K')

    Returns:
        A decimal representation of file size

        Examples::

            >>> size_to_bytes("500")
            500
            >>> size_to_bytes("1K")
            1000
    """
    size = size.replace(',', '').replace(' ', '')
    unit = size[-1].lower()
    if unit == 'k':
        return int(size[:-1]) * 1024
    elif unit == 'm':
        return int(size[:-1]) * 1024 * 1024
    elif unit == 'g':
        return int(size[:-1]) * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
    elif unit == 't':
        return int(size[:-1]) * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown unit '{unit}' in file size '{size}'")
```

```python
import re

def size_to_bytes(size: str) -> int:
    """Convert human readable file size to bytes.

    Resulting value is an approximation as input value is in most case rounded.

    Args:
        size: A string representing a human readable file size (eg: '500K')

    Returns:
        A decimal representation of file size

        Examples::

            >>> size_to_bytes("500")
            500
            >>> size_to_bytes("1K")
            1000
    """
    size_units = {
        'K': 1024,
        'M': 1024**2,
        'G': 1024**3,
        'T': 1024**4,
    }
    
    match = re.match(r'(\d+(\.\d+)?)\s*([KMGT])', size)
    if match:
        value = float(match.group(1))
        unit = match.group(3).upper()
        return int(value * size_units[unit])
    else:
        raise ValueError('Invalid file size format')
```

```python
def vertex3tuple(vertices):
    # Check if the input is a list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a vertex
    if not all(isinstance(v, dict) and 'x' in v and 'y' in v for v in vertices):
        return "Invalid input. Expected a list of dictionaries with 'x' and 'y' keys."

    # Convert the list of vertices to a list of tuples
    vertices = [(v['x'], v['y']) for v in vertices]

    # Calculate the 3D vertices for each vertex
    result = []
    for i in range(len(vertices)):
        x1, y1 = vertices[i]
        x2, y2 = vertices[(i+1) % len(vertices)]
        x3, y3 = vertices[(i+2) % len(vertices)]
        result.append(((x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3)))

    return result
```

```python
def int_to_string(number: int, alphabet: List[str], padding: Optional[int] = None) -> str:
    """
    Convert a number to a string, using the given alphabet.

    The output has the most significant digit first.
    """
    if not isinstance(number, int):
        raise ValueError("Input must be an integer.")
    if not isinstance(alphabet, list) or not alphabet:
        raise ValueError("Alphabet must be a non-empty list.")
    
    if padding is not None and (number < 0 or padding < 0):
        raise ValueError("Padding must be non-negative for non-negative numbers.")
    
    negative = number < 0
    number = abs(number)
    result = ""
    
    while number > 0:
        remainder = number % len(alphabet)
        result = alphabet[remainder] + result
        number //= len(alphabet)
    
    if negative:
        result = '-' + result
    
    if padding is not None:
        padding_width = padding - len(result)
        result = '0' * padding_width + result
    
    return result
```

```python
    Convert a number to a string, using the given alphabet.

    if padding is not None:
```

```python
    The output has the most significant digit first.

    if number < 0:
```

```python
    if number >= len(alphabet):
        raise ValueError("Number is too large to be represented by the given alphabet")

    result = ""

    if padding is not None:
```

```python
def string_to_int(string: str, alphabet: List[str]) -> int:
    """
    Convert a string to a number, using the given alphabet.

    The input is assumed to have the most significant digit first.
    """
    value = 0
    A = ord('A')
    Z = ord('Z')
    for i, c in enumerate(string):
        if c not in alphabet:
```

```python
    The input is assumed to have the most significant digit first.
    """
    base = len(alphabet)
    result = 0
    power = 1

    for char in reversed(string):
        position = alphabet.index(char)
        result += position * power
        power *= base

    return result
```

```python
from datetime import timedelta

def parse_frequency(frequency):
    if frequency is None or frequency.lower() == 'always':
        return None

    units = {
        'year': 365,
        'month': 30,
        'week': 7,
        'day': 1,
        'hour': 1 / 24,
        'minute': 1 / (24 * 60),
        'second': 1 / (24 * 60 * 60)
    }

    num = float(frequency[:-1])
    unit = frequency[-1]

    if unit not in units:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported unit '{unit}' in frequency '{frequency}'")

    timedelta_num = num * units[unit]

    return timedelta(seconds=timedelta_num)
```

```python
import re

def make_find_paths(find_paths):
    '''Given a sequence of path fragments or patterns as passed to `--find`, transform all path
    fragments into glob patterns. Pass through existing patterns untouched.

    For example, given find_paths of:

      ['foo.txt', 'pp:root/somedir']

    ... transform that into:

      ['sh:**/*foo.txt*/**', 'pp:root/somedir']
    '''
    new_paths = []
    for path in find_paths:
        if re.search(r'\*\*', path):  # handle glob patterns
            new_paths.extend(re.findall(r'([^\*\*\*\]*)\*\*', path))
        else:
            new_paths.append(path)
    return new_paths
```

```python
    fragments into glob patterns. Pass through existing patterns untouched.

    For example, given find_paths of:

      ['foo.txt', 'pp:root/somedir']
```

```python
    If the variable is not defined in the environment and no default value is provided, an Error is raised.
```

```python
    """
    Iterate over a string list and remove trailing os seperator characters.

    Each string is tested if its length is greater than one and if the last
    character is the pathname seperator. If so, the pathname seperator character
    is removed.

    Args:
        input_list: list of strings

    Returns:
        Processed list of strings

    Raises:
        TypeError
    """
    if not isinstance(input_list, list):
        raise TypeError("Input must be a list")

    processed_list = []
    for item in input_list:
        if item is None:
           processed_list.append(item)
            continue

        if len(item) <= 1:
            processed_list.append(item)
            continue

        last_char = item[-1]

        if os.path.isdir(last_char):
            processed_list.append(item[:-1])
        else:
            processed_list.append(item)

    return processed_list
```

```python
def find_roots(graph: "Graph", prop: "URIRef", roots: Optional[Set["Node"]] = None) -> Set["Node"]:
    """Find the roots in some sort of transitive hierarchy.

    find_roots(graph, rdflib.RDFS.subClassOf)
    will return a set of all roots of the sub-class hierarchy

    Assumes triple of the form (child, prop, parent), i.e. the direction of
    RDFS.subClassOf or SKOS.broader

    """
    if roots is None:
        roots = set()

    for s, p, o in graph.triples((None, prop, None)):
        if p == rdflib.RDFS.subClassOf or p == rdflib.URIRef('http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#broader'):
            roots.add(s)

    return roots
```

```python
from rdflib import Graph, URIRef, Node

def find_roots(graph: Graph, prop: URIRef, roots: Optional[Set[Node]] = None) -> Set[Node]:
    """
    Find the roots in some sort of transitive hierarchy.

    find_roots(graph, rdflib.RDFS.subClassOf)
    will return a set of all roots of the sub-class hierarchy

    Assumes triple of the form (child, prop, parent), i.e. the direction of
    RDFS.subClassOf or SKOS.broader

    """

    if roots is None:
        roots = set()

    # Extract individuals and their parents
    individuals = list(graph.subjects(prop, None))
    for ind in individuals:
        parents = list(graph.predecessors(ind))
        for parent in parents:
            roots.add(parent)

    return roots
```

```python
        :param tz: optional timezone
```

```python
            raise ValueError(f"ticks must be between 0 and 86400000000000 inclusive, got {ticks}")
```

```python
    """Get or set the scale of the graph.

    If *other* is ``None``, return the scale of this graph.

    If a numeric *other* is provided, rescale to that value.
    If the graph has unknown or zero scale,
    rescaling that will raise :exc:`~.LenaValueError`.

    To get meaningful results, graph's fields are used.
    Only the last coordinate is rescaled.
    For example, if the graph has *x* and *y* coordinates,
    then *y* will be rescaled, and for a 3-dimensional graph
    *z* will be rescaled.
    All errors are rescaled together with their coordinate.
    """
    if other is None:
        return self.scale
    elif isinstance(other, (int, float)):
        new_scale = other
    else:
        raise ValueError("Invalid scale value")

    if self.scale == 0:
        raise LenaValueError("Unknown or zero scale")
    self.scale *= new_scale

    for attr in self.__dict__:
        if attr in ['x', 'y', 'z']:
            setattr(self, attr, self.__dict__[attr] * new_scale)
```

```python
    a named tuple with fields *mean*, *mean_error* and a context
    one could use

    *get_coordinate* defines what the coordinate

    It can be "left" (default), "right" and "middle".

    *field_names* set field names of the graph. Their number
    must be the same as the dimension of the result.
    For a *make_value* above they would be
    *("x", "y_mean", "y_mean_error")*.

    *scale* becomes the graph's scale (unknown by default).
    If it is ``True``, it uses the histogram scale.

    *hist* must contain only numeric bins (without context)
    or *make_value* must remove context when creating a numeric graph.

    Return the resulting graph.
    """
    assert all(isinstance(b, (int, float)) for b in hist)
    if not make_value:
        make_value = lambda bin_: bin_

    if scale is None:
        scale = True
    elif not scale:
        raise ValueError('scale can only be None or True')

    x = np.linspace(1, len(hist), len(hist))
    if get_coordinate.lower() == "right":
        x = x[-1::-1]

    y = [make_value(b) for b in hist]
    if scale:
        y = [y[i] * len(hist) for i in range(len(y))]
```

```python
                  field_names=("x", "y"), scale=None):

    *make_value* is a function to set the value of a graph's point.
    By default it is bin content.
    *make_value* accepts a single value (bin content) without context.

    This option could be used to create graph's error bars.

    from a histogram where bins contain

    one could use

    >>> make_value = lambda bin_: (bin_.mean, bin_.mean_error)

    *get_coordinate* defines what the coordinate
```

```python
    *field_names* set field names of the graph. Their number
    must be the same as the dimension of the result.
    For a *make_value* above they would be
    *("x", "y_mean", "y_mean_error")*.

    *scale* becomes the graph's scale (unknown by default).
    If it is ``True``, it uses the histogram scale.

    *hist* must contain only numeric bins (without context)
    or *make_value* must remove context when creating a numeric graph.

    Return the resulting graph.
    """
    import numpy as np
    from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Tuple
    from .histogram import Histogram
    from .item import Item
    from .graph import Graph
    from .attributes import Attribute

    def _get_x_coordinate(bin_: Histogram) -> float:
        if get_coordinate == "left":
            return bin_.left
        elif get_coordinate == "right":
            return bin_.right
        elif get_coordinate == "middle":
            return (bin_.left + bin_.right) / 2
        else:
            raise ValueError("Invalid get_coordinate value. Must be one of 'left', 'right', or 'middle'.")

    def _make_value(bin_: Histogram) -> float:
        if make_value is None:
            return bin_.count
        elif callable(make_value):
            return make_value(bin_.count)
        else:
            raise ValueError("make_value must be a callable that accepts a single value (bin content) without context.")

    def _get_y_coordinate(bin_: Histogram) -> float:
        return bin_.bincontent

    def _create_graph_points(hist: Histogram, make_value: Callable, field_names: Tuple, scale: bool) -> List[Tuple]:
        points = []
        for bin_ in hist:
            value = _make_value(bin_)
            if value is None:
                raise ValueError("make_value returned None for histogram bin")

            x_coordinate = _get_x_coordinate(bin_)
            y_coordinate = _get_y_coordinate(bin_)

            points.append((x_coordinate, y_coordinate, value))
        return points

    def _create_graph(hist: Histogram, field_names: Tuple, scale: bool) -> Graph:
        if scale:
            scale_value = _get_y_coordinate(hist)
        else:
            scale_value = 1

        points = _create_graph_points(hist, _make_value, field_names, scale)
        graph = Graph(field_names=field_names, points=points, scale_value=scale_value)
        return graph

    if not isinstance(hist, Histogram):
```

```python
def hist_to_graph(hist, make_value=None, get_coordinate="left",
                  field_names=("x", "y"), scale=None):
    """Convert a :class:`.histogram` to a :class:`.graph`.

    *make_value* is a function to set the value of a graph's point.
    By default it is bin content.
    *make_value* accepts a single value (bin content) without context.

    This option could be used to create graph's error bars.
    For example, to create a graph with errors
    from a histogram where bins contain
    a named tuple with fields *mean*, *mean_error* and a context
    one could use

    >>> make_value = lambda bin_: (bin_.mean, bin_.mean_error)

    *get_coordinate* defines what the coordinate
    of a graph point created from a histogram bin will be.
    It can be "left" (default), "right" and "middle".

    *field_names* set field names of the graph. Their number
    must be the same as the dimension of the result.
    For a *make_value* above they would be
    *("x", "y_mean", "y_mean_error")*.

    *scale* becomes the graph's scale (unknown by default).
    If it is ``True``, it uses the histogram scale.

    *hist* must contain only numeric bins (without context)
    or *make_value* must remove context when creating a numeric graph.

    Return the resulting graph.
    """
    if scale is True:
        scale = hist.scale
    
    data = []
    for i, bin_ in enumerate(hist):
        if scale is True:
            value = bin_.count
        else:
            value = make_value(bin_)
        x = hist.get_coordinate(i, get_coordinate)
        field_vals = [x] + [value]
        data.append(field_vals)
    
    # Assuming graph creation logic goes here
    graph = Graph(field_names)
    graph.add_points(data)
    return graph
```

```python
def _verify(iface, candidate, tentative=False, vtype=None):
    """
    Verify that *candidate* might correctly provide *iface*.

    This involves:

    - Making sure the candidate claims that it provides the
      interface using ``iface.providedBy`` (unless *tentative* is `True`,
      in which case this step is skipped). This means that the candidate's class
      declares that it `implements <zope.interface.implementer>` the interface,
      or the candidate itself declares that it `provides <zope.interface.provider>`
      the interface

    - Making sure the candidate defines all the necessary methods

    - Making sure the methods have the correct signature (to the
      extent possible)

    - Making sure the candidate defines all the necessary attributes

    :return bool: Returns a true value if everything that could be
       checked passed.
    :raises zope.interface.Invalid: If any of the previous
       conditions does not hold.

    .. versionchanged:: 5.0
        If multiple methods or attributes are invalid, all such errors
        are collected and reported. Previously, only the first error was reported.
        As a special case, if only one such error is present, it is raised
        alone, like before.
    """
    if tentative:
        # No need to check if the candidate claims to provide the interface
        return True

    # Verify interface claim
    if not iface.providedBy(candidate):
        raise zope.interface.Invalid(f" Interface {iface} is not provided by {candidate}")

    # Verify existence of required methods
    missing_methods = [method for method in iface.implementedBy(candidate) if hasattr(candidate, method) == False]
    if missing_methods:
        if len(missing_methods) == 1:
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f" Missing required method: {missing_methods[0]}")
        else:
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f" Missing required methods: {', '.join(missing_methods)}")

    # Verify correct signature of methods
    for method in iface.implementedBy(candidate):
        if hasattr(candidate, method):
            method_signature = inspect.signature(getattr(candidate, method)).parameters
            if method_signature != iface.methods[method]:
                raise zope.interface.Invalid(f" Method {method} has incorrect signature")

    # Verify existence of required attributes
    missing_attributes = [attr for attr in iface.attributes if not hasattr(candidate, attr) == False]
    if missing_attributes:
        if len(missing_attributes) == 1:
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f" Missing required attribute: {missing_attributes[0]}")
        else:
            raise zope.interface.Invalid(f" Missing required attributes: {', '.join(missing_attributes)}")

    return True
```

```python
      declares that it `implements <zope.interface.implementer>` the interface,

      the interface

    - Making sure the candidate defines all the necessary methods

        If multiple methods or attributes are invalid, all such errors
        are collected and reported. Previously, only the first error was reported.
        As a special case, if only one such error is present, it is raised
        alone, like before.
    """
```

```python
        candidates = iface.providedBy(candidate)
        if tentative and candidates:
            raise Invalid(str(candidates))
        elif not tentative:
            possible_implementations = []
            for a in iface with RespectGrandparents=True:
                for i in a.__implementors__:
                    for c in a.__implemented_interfaces__:
                        if c == iface:
                            possible_implementations.append(c)
            if possible_implementations:
                raise Invalid("Candidate is not implemented by any interface."
                             " It would either have to import the interface into the class"
                             " definition node, about the following possible implementations:"
                             " " + "\n".join([str(i) for i in possible_implementations]))
            else:
                raise Invalid("Candidate is not implementing <zope.interface.implementer> "
                             "or <zope.interface.provider> the interface "
                             str(iface) + " in any way."
                             )

    missing_methods = []
    for method_name in dir(iface):
        if method_name.startswith('__') or method_name == 'providedBy' or method_name == 'factory':
            continue
        if not hasattr(candidate, method_name):
            missing_methods.append(method_name)

    if missing_methods:
        if len(missing_methods) == 1 or tentative:
            exception_class = Invalid
            extra_text = "The missing method is: "
        else:
            exception_class = DuplicateAnnotationError
            extra_text = "The missing methods are: "
        raise exception_class(extra_text + "\n".join([str(method) for method in missing_methods]))

    if vtype and hasattr(candidate, 'tl'):
        if candidate.tl is None:
            raise Invalid("The candidate must provide the tlv value "
                         "using \\tl tag.")
        if not isinstance(candidate.tl, vtype):
            raise Invalid("The provided tlv value is not of type " + str(vtype) + ".")

    return True
```

```python
import re
from typing import Pattern

def _create_in_regex(self) -> Pattern:
    """Create the in-style parameter regular expression.

    Returns the in-style parameter regular expression (:class:`re.Pattern`).
    """
    qname, attrs = self.raw.qname, self.attrs
    extra_attrs = self.extra_attrs

    # start pegging at the start of a line
    in_regex = r'^' if not qname.startswith('\\/') else r''
    # we must have an identifier at the start of a line
    in_regex += r'(?P<identifier>[\w:]+)'

    if attrs:
        # we have attributes, peg these after the identifier identifier
        in_regex += r'\t(?P<arguments>([^\t]+(?:\t[^\t]+)*))'

    # finish out with the terminator, when we have found a match we're done.
    in_regex += r'(?P<tok>=$)'
    return re.compile(in_regex)
```

```python
    standard. Incomplete date formats (such as ``YYYY-MM``) may *not* be
    combined with a time portion.

    Supported date formats are:

    Common:

    - ``YYYY``
    - ``YYYY-MM`` or ``YYYYMM``
    - ``YYYY-MM-DD`` or ``YYYYMMDD``

    Uncommon:

    - ``YYYY-Www`` or ``YYYYWww`` - ISO week (day defaults to 0)
    - ``YYYY-Www-D`` or ``YYYYWwwD`` - ISO week and day

    The ISO week and day numbering follows the same logic as
    :func:`datetime.date.isocalendar`.

    Supported time formats are:

    - ``hh``
    - ``hh:mm`` or ``hhmm``
    - ``hh:mm:ss`` or ``hhmmss``
    - ``hh:mm:ss.ssssss`` (Up to 6 sub-second digits)

    Midnight is a special case for `hh`, as the standard supports both
    00:00 and 24:00 as a representation. The decimal separator can be
    either a dot or a comma.


    .. caution::

            Support for fractional components other than seconds is part of the
            ISO-8601 standard, but is not currently implemented in this parser.

        Supported time zone offset formats are:

        - `Z` (UTC)
        - `±HH:MM`
        - `±HHMM`
        - `±HH`

        Offsets will be represented as :class:`dateutil.tz.tzoffset` objects,
        with the exception of UTC, which will be represented as
        :class:`dateutil.tz.tzutc`. Time zone offsets equivalent to UTC (such
        as `+00:00`) will also be represented as :class:`dateutil.tz.tzutc`.

        :param dt_str:
            A string or stream containing only an ISO-8601 datetime string

        :return:
            Returns a :class:`datetime.datetime` representing the string.
            Unspecified components default to their lowest value.

        .. warning::

            As of version 2.7.0, the strictness of the parser should not be
            considered a stable part of the contract. Any valid ISO-8601 string
            that parses correctly with the default settings will continue to
            parse correctly in future versions, but invalid strings that
            currently fail (e.g. ``2017-01-01T00:00+00:00:00``) are not
            guaranteed to continue failing in future versions if they encode
            a valid date.

        .. versionadded:: 2.7.0
    """
    dt_str = dt_str.rstrip()
    # Splitting the date and time parts and removing the time zone if present
    date_part, time_part = dt_str.split('T', 1) if 'T' in dt_str else (dt_str, '')

    # Parsing the date
    year, month, day = int(date_part[:4]), int(date_part[4:6]), int(date_part[6:8])
    dt = datetime(year, month, day)

    # Parsing the time
    if time_part:
        time_part = time_part.rstrip()
        hour, minute, second = time_part[:2], time_part[2:4], time_part[4:6]
        if '.' in second:
            second, microsecond = second.split('.')
            second = int(second)
            microsecond = int(microsecond)
        else:
            second, microsecond = int(second), 0
        datetime_format = "%H%M%S.%6f" if len(second) > 2 and len(microsecond) > 0 else "%H%M%S.%f"
        dt = dt.replace(hour=int(hour), minute=int(minute), second=int(second), microsecond=microsecond)

    # Parsing the time zone
    if date_part[-1] == 'Z':
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=dateutil.tz.tzutc())
    elif date_part[-2:] in ['-00', '+00']:
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=dateutil.tz.tzoffset("", 0))
    elif date_part[-2:] == "±.HH" or date_part[-4:] == "±HHMM":
        sign = "+" if date_part[-2:] == "±.HH" else "-"
        h, m = map(int, date_part[-4:-2])
        dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=dateutil.tz.tzoffset(sign, h * 3600 + m * 60))
    elif date_part[-5:] == "±HHDD" or date_part[-7:] == "±HHMMDD":
        sign = "+" if date_part[-5:] == "±HHDD" else "-"
        h, d = map(int, date_part[-5:-3])
        datetime_format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%6f"
        dt = dt.replace(year=year + h, month=month, day=day).replace(tzinfo=dateutil.tz.tzoffset(sign, (h * 24 + d - 1) * 3600))

    return dt
```

```python
def isoparse(dt_str):

    dt_str = dt_str.strip()

    try:
        # if the string is empty, return None
        if not dt_str:
            return None

        # split the string into date and time parts, separated by the 'T' character
        parts = dt_str.split('T')
        if len(parts) == 2:
            date_str = parts[0]
            time_str = parts[1]
        elif len(parts) == 1:
            date_str = parts[0]
            time_str = '00:00:00'
        else:
            raise ValueError("Invalid ISO-8601 datetime string")

        # if the date part is missing or empty, set it to the current date
        date_part = None
        if date_str:
            if len(date_str) >= 4:
                year = int(date_str[:4])
                month = int(date_str[4:6]) if len(date_str) >= 6 else 1
                day = int(date_str[6:8]) if len(date_str) >= 8 else 1
                date_part = datetime(year, month, day)
            elif len(parts[0]) == 2:
                year = int(date_str[:2])
                month = int(date_str[2:4]) if len(date_str) >= 4 else 1
                date_part = datetime(year, month, 1)
            elif len(parts[0]) == 4:
                year = int(date_str[:4])
                date_part = datetime(year, 1, 1)
            else:
                raise ValueError("Invalid date format")
        else:
            date_part = datetime.now()

        # if the time part is missing or empty, set it to the current time
        time_part = None
        if time_str:
            if len(time_str) >= 2:
                hour = int(time_str[:2])
                minute = int(time_str[2:4])
                second = int(time_str[4:6]) if len(time_str) >= 6 else 0
                microsecond = int(time_str[6:13]) if len(time_str) >= 13 else 0
                time_part = datetime(0, 0, 0, hour, minute, second, microsecond)
            elif len(parts[1]) == 2:
                hour = int(time_str[:2])
                minute = int(time_str[2:4])
                time_part = datetime(0, 0, 0, hour, minute, 0)
            elif len(parts[1]) == 4:
                hour = int(time_str[:4])
                time_part = datetime(0, 0, 0, hour, 0, 0)
            else:
                raise ValueError("Invalid time format")

        # combine the date and time parts to form the desired datetime object
        if date_part and time_part:
            dt = datetime.combine(date_part, time_part)
        elif date_part:
            dt = date_part
        else:
            dt = datetime.now()

        # if there is a time zone offset part, parse it and add it to the datetime object
        if '+' in dt_str or '-' in dt_str:
            tz_str = dt_str[dt_str.find('+'):dt_str.find('Z') + 1]
            hours, minutes = map(int, tz_str.split(':'))
            if tz_str.startswith('-'):
                hours *= -1
                minutes *= -1
            tz_offset = datetime.timedelta(hours=hours, minutes=minutes)
            dt = dt + tz_offset

        # return the parse datetime object
        return dt

    except (ValueError, IndexError):
        raise ValueError("Invalid ISO-8601 datetime string")
```

```python
import re

def isoparse(dt_str):
    """
    Parse an ISO-8601 datetime string into a :class:`datetime.datetime`.

    An ISO-8601 datetime string consists of a date portion, followed
    optionally by a time portion - the date and time portions are separated
    by a single character separator, which is ``T`` in the official
    standard. Incomplete date formats (such as ``YYYY-MM``) may *not* be
    combined with a time portion.

    Supported date formats are:

    Common:

    - ``YYYY``
    - ``YYYY-MM`` or ``YYYYMM``
    - ``YYYY-MM-DD`` or ``YYYYMMDD``

    Uncommon:

    - ``YYYY-Www`` or ``YYYYWww`` - ISO week (day defaults to 0)
    - ``YYYY-Www-D`` or ``YYYYWwwD`` - ISO week and day

    The ISO week and day numbering follows the same logic as
    :func:`datetime.date.isocalendar`.

    Supported time formats are:

    - ``hh``
    - ``hh:mm`` or ``hhmm``
    - ``hh:mm:ss`` or ``hhmmss``
    - ``hh:mm:ss.ssssss`` (Up to 6 sub-second digits)

    Midnight is a special case for `hh`, as the standard supports both
    00:00 and 24:00 as a representation. The decimal separator can be
    either a dot or a comma.

    :param dt_str:
        A string or stream containing only an ISO-8601 datetime string

    :return:
        Returns a :class:`datetime.datetime` representing the string.
        Unspecified components default to their lowest value.

    .. warning::

            As of version 2.7.0, the strictness of the parser should not be
            considered a stable part of the contract. Any valid ISO-8601 string
            that parses correctly with the default settings will continue to
            parse correctly in future versions, but invalid strings that
            currently fail (e.g. ``2017-01-01T00:00+00:00:00``) are not
            guaranteed to continue failing in future versions if they encode
            a valid date.
    """
    
    dt_str = dt_str.strip()
    
    # validate the datetime format
    match = re.match(r'^(\d{4}(?:-\d{2}(?:-\d{2})?)|(\d{4}-W\d{2}(?:-\d{1})?)|(\d{4}-W\d{2})|(\d{4}(?:-\d{2})?T\d{2}(\:\d{2}(\:\d{2}(?:\.\d{6})?)?)?)((?:Z|-\d{2}:\d{2}|-\d{2}\.\d{2})?)$', dt_str)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid ISO-8601 datetime string: {dt_str}")
    
    components = match.groups()
    
    # parse the date part
    year = int(components[0])
    month = int(components[1]) if components[1] else None
    day = int(components[2]) if components[2] else None
    if month and day:
        date = datetime(year, month, day)
    else:
        year_str = components[0].replace("-", "")
        if len(year_str) in range(2, 6):
            year = int(year_str)
            month = 1
            day = None
        else:
            month = int(components[1])
            day = int(components[2]).replace("-", "")
    
    # parse the time part
    time_str = components[3] if components[3] else "00:00:00"
    if time_str[2] == ":":
        time_str += ":00"
    time = datetime.strptime(time_str, "%H:%M:%S").time()
    
    # parse the time zone offset
    offset = components[5] if components[5] else "+00:00"
    if offset in ["Z", "+00:00"]:
        tz = datetime.tzutc()
    elif offset[0] == "-":
        tz = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=int(offset[1:2]), minutes=int(offset[3:5])), offset[1:2] + offset[3:5]] if len(offset) == 5 else datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=int(offset[1:])), "+0" + offset[1:])
    else:
        tz = datetime.timezone(datetime.timedelta(hours=int(offset[:-2]), minutes=int(offset[-2:])), offset[:-2] + offset[-2:])
    
    # combine the date, time, and time zone offset
    dt = datetime.combine(date, time, tz)
    
    return dt
```

```python
    """
    Given a timezone-aware datetime in a given timezone, calculates a
    timezone-aware datetime in a new timezone.

    Since this is the one time that we *know* we have an unambiguous
    datetime object, we take this opportunity to determine whether the
    datetime is ambiguous and in a "fold" state (e.g. if it's the first
    occurrence, chronologically, of the ambiguous datetime).

    :param dt:
            A timezone-aware :class:`datetime.datetime` object.
    """
    tzinfo = dt.tzinfo
    dt = dt.astimezone(tzinfo)
    utcfmt = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ%z"
    utctimestr = dt.strftime(utcfmt)
    utc_dt = dt.tzinfo.localize(utctimestr)
    print(utc_dt)
```

```python
        ``dt`` if (and only if) it is naive.
```

def find_tags(text, replacer=None):
    """Find tags in text.

    Tries to ignore tags inside code blocks.

    Optionally, if passed a "replacer", will also replace the tag word with the result
    of the replacer function called with the tag word.

    Returns a set of tags and the original or replaced text.
    """
    tags = set()
    marked = False
    pos = -1

    i = 0
    while i < len(text):
        if text[i:i+3] == '```':
            marked = not marked
            i += 3
            continue
        if marked:
            i += 1
            continue
        if text[i:i+2] == '[[':

            if i == -1:
                i = len(text)
            if pos != -1:
               .tags.add(text[pos:i+2])
            pos = i + 2
        i += 1

    if pos != -1:
        tags.add(text[pos:-1])

    if replacer:
        text = text.replace('[[' * 2, tolower(text))
        text = text.replace(']]' * 2, ']]' * 2)

    return tags, text

```python
def find_tags(text: str, replacer: Callable = None) -> Tuple[Set, str]:
    """Find tags in text.

    Tries to ignore tags inside code blocks.

    Optionally, if passed a "replacer", will also replace the tag word with the result
    of the replacer function called with the tag word.

    Returns a set of tags and the original or replaced text.
    """
    tags = set()
    previous_tag = None

    for match in re.finditer(r"(\{[^{}]*\})", text):
        [tag] = match.groups()
        if previous_tag is not None:
            if tag != previous_tag:
                tags.add(previous_tag)
        tags.add(tag)
        previous_tag = tag

    modified_text = text
    if replacer:
        modified_text = re.sub(r"(\{[^{}]*\})", lambda match: replacer(match.group(1)), modified_text)

    return tags, modified_text
```

            code_start = max(0, start + 1)
            code_end = min(text.find('```', code_end), text.find('```', code_start) + 3 - len(text)) # position at start of actual code block
            
            # recursively call find_tags within the code block
            found_tags, replaced_text = find_tags(text[start_end + 3:code_start], replacer)
            tags.update(found_tags)
            text = text[:start_end + 3] + replaced_text + text[code_start + 3:]
            
        # if a replacer is provided, replace the tag word with the result of the replacer function
        if replacer is not None:
            text = text[:start] + replacer(tag) + text[start + len(tag):]
        
    if start != -1:  # check again for any remaining tags
            tags.add(text[start+1:start])
    
    return tags, text

```python
from typing import Tuple, Set

def find_tags(text: str, replacer: callable = None) -> Tuple[Set, str]:
    """Find tags in text.

    Tries to ignore tags inside code blocks.

    Optionally, if passed a "replacer", will also replace the tag word with the result
    of the replacer function called with the tag word.

    Returns a set of tags and the original or replaced text.
    """
    tags = set()
    current_tag = None
    in_code_block = False

    for char in text:
        if char == '<':
            if current_tag is None:
                current_tag = ''
            in_code_block = True
        elif current_tag:
            if char == '>':
                in_code_block = False
                if replacer:
                    current_tag = replacer(current_tag)
                tags.add(current_tag)
                current_tag = None
            else:
                current_tag += char

    return tags, text
```

```python
    try:
```

```python
        status_code = response.status_code
        error = response.raise_for_status()
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout:
```

```python
def get_nested_custom_and_control_args(args):
    """Split input arguments to control nested and custom.

    Controls arguments: control the IR behavior. These arguments
        will not be put into the spec yml file
    Nested arguments: are used by the Ansible playbooks and will be put
        into the spec yml file.
    Custom arguments: Custom ansible variables to be used instead of the
        normal nested usage.

    :param args: the collected list of args.
    :return: (dict, dict): flat dicts (control_args, nested_args)
    """
    control_args = {}
    nested_args = {}

    for arg in args:
        if arg.startswith("--custom-args-"):
            custom_arg, value = arg.split("=")
            custom_args[custom_arg] = value
        elif arg.startswith("--nested-args-"):
            nested_arg, value = arg.split("=")
            nested_args[nested_arg] = value
        else:
            control_args[arg] = value

    return control_args, nested_args
```
